message.content:
You are reviewing an uncommitted diff in the andesim repo (a RISC-V hybrid simulator C++ driver). Do NOT look for correctness bugs - only REUSE issues: new code that re-implements something the codebase already has. Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change, and name the existing helper to call instead.

Repo context (grep freely):
- driver/state_diff.cpp / state_diff.hpp - the `--verify` oracle differential compare. `diff_states()` compares two `hybrid_state_v1` structs. `andes_verify_excluded(name)` is a lambda returning true for CSR names that `--verify` skips. There's a parallel `andes_supported_csr(name)` lambda.
- include/hybrid/state_abi.h - `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` X-macro defines 13 Andes CSRs; `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` is a similar list.
- driver/state_diff_test.cpp - unit tests using a custom `CHECK()` macro (driver/test_check.hpp) and `test::report`.
- tests/andes_sim/*.sh - shell contract tests; they source tests/lib/log.sh (provides `fail`/`ok`/`cfg_val`/`vsim_bin_dir`).

Return findings as a list, each with: file, line (from the diff), one-line summary, concrete cost (what is duplicated, and the existing helper to call). If there is nothing to flag, say "clean" and stop. Be concise; this is a ~50-line diff.

THE DIFF UNDER REVIEW:

```diff
diff --git a/driver/state_diff.cpp b/driver/state_diff.cpp
@@ andes_verify_excluded lambda @@
     // msp_bound/msp_base: engine-reset-divergent HW stack-protection bounds.
+    // milmb/mdlmb: ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs. The base address round-trips, but
+    // the enable bit (bit 0) is HW-presence state -- the vsim RTL has the local
+    // memories and drains EN=1, while QEMU models none and drains EN=0. Same
+    // class as msp_bound/msp_base (an engine-implementation artifact, not a
+    // transport bug), so excluded rather than half-compared via a bit mask.
     // mhpmcounter3..6: ...
     return name == "msp_bound" || name == "msp_base" ||
+           name == "milmb" || name == "mdlmb" ||
            name == "mhpmcounter3" || name == "mhpmcounter4" ||
            name == "mhpmcounter5" || name == "mhpmcounter6" ||
            name == "mdcause" || name == "tdata1" ||
            name == "tcontrol" || name == "mcontext";

diff --git a/driver/state_diff_test.cpp b/driver/state_diff_test.cpp
-// Andes block compared fields: 13 scalars - 2 verify-excluded (msp_bound,
-// msp_base; ...) + pmacfg[2] + pmaaddr[16] = 29.
+// Andes block compared fields: 13 scalars - 4 verify-excluded (msp_bound,
+// msp_base, milmb, mdlmb; ...) + pmacfg[2] + pmaaddr[16] = 27.
 constexpr int kAndesCompared =
-    (13 - 2) + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
+    (13 - 4) + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
@@ probe array @@
-      {"milmb", &hybrid_andes_csr::milmb},          // F5
+      {"mecc_code", &hybrid_andes_csr::mecc_code},  // F5 memory system
@@ new test block @@
+  {  // milmb/mdlmb are the ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs ... verify EXCLUDES them
+    const hybrid_state_v1 ref = andes_state();
+    hybrid_state_v1 got = ref;
+    got.andes.milmb ^= 0x1;  // flip the enable bit only (base unchanged)
+    got.andes.mdlmb ^= 0x1;
+    CHECK(diff_states(ref, got).ok());
+  }
```

Also `git diff HEAD -- driver/ tests/` in /home/nick/work/andesim for full context (the shell test tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh also added two hybrid blocks mirroring its cycle blocks).

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

diff --git a/driver/state_diff.cpp b/driver/state_diff.cpp
index dc3e8db..57d1b8f 100644
--- a/driver/state_diff.cpp
+++ b/driver/state_diff.cpp
@@ -93,6 +93,11 @@ DiffReport diff_states(const hybrid_state_v1& ref, const hybrid_state_v1& got,
   // like mip's hardware-driven pending bits.
   auto andes_verify_excluded = [](std::string_view name) {
     // msp_bound/msp_base: engine-reset-divergent HW stack-protection bounds.
+    // milmb/mdlmb: ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs. The base address round-trips, but
+    // the enable bit (bit 0) is HW-presence state -- the vsim RTL has the local
+    // memories and drains EN=1, while QEMU models none and drains EN=0. Same
+    // class as msp_bound/msp_base (an engine-implementation artifact, not a
+    // transport bug), so excluded rather than half-compared via a bit mask.
     // mhpmcounter3..6: hardware performance counters that increment DURING the
     // ROI, so the vsim (cycle) and QEMU (functional) values legitimately differ
     // -- transported and restored, but not strict-compared, like mcycle/mip.
@@ -101,6 +106,7 @@ DiffReport diff_states(const hybrid_state_v1& ref, const hybrid_state_v1& got,
     // WARL widths differ between QEMU and vsim. All transported + restored, but
     // not cross-engine strict-compared.
     return name == "msp_bound" || name == "msp_base" ||
+           name == "milmb" || name == "mdlmb" ||
            name == "mhpmcounter3" || name == "mhpmcounter4" ||
            name == "mhpmcounter5" || name == "mhpmcounter6" ||
            name == "mdcause" || name == "tdata1" ||
diff --git a/driver/state_diff_test.cpp b/driver/state_diff_test.cpp
index 26f27c5..f3d6b49 100644
--- a/driver/state_diff_test.cpp
+++ b/driver/state_diff_test.cpp
@@ -71,11 +71,11 @@ hybrid_state_v1 andes_state() {
   return s;
 }
 
-// Andes block compared fields: 13 scalars - 2 verify-excluded (msp_bound,
-// msp_base; engine-reset-divergent, see state_diff.cpp) + pmacfg[2] +
-// pmaaddr[16] = 29.
+// Andes block compared fields: 13 scalars - 4 verify-excluded (msp_bound,
+// msp_base, milmb, mdlmb; engine-reset-divergent, see state_diff.cpp) +
+// pmacfg[2] + pmaaddr[16] = 27.
 constexpr int kAndesCompared =
-    (13 - 2) + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
+    (13 - 4) + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
 
 }  // namespace
 
@@ -283,14 +283,15 @@ int main() {
     CHECK(r.compared == 6 + 32 + 5 + kAndesCompared);  // base RV64 set + andes
   }
 
-  {  // each representative Andes CSR (one per feature F1..F8) is caught + named
+  {  // each representative COMPARED Andes CSR is caught + named (milmb/mdlmb are
+     // verify-excluded -- see the dedicated block above)
     const hybrid_state_v1 ref = andes_state();
     const std::pair<const char*, uint64_t hybrid_andes_csr::*> probes[] = {
       {"uitb", &hybrid_andes_csr::uitb},            // F1 CoDense
       {"jvt", &hybrid_andes_csr::jvt},              // F1 Zcmt
       {"mxstatus", &hybrid_andes_csr::mxstatus},    // F2
       {"ucode", &hybrid_andes_csr::ucode},          // F4 DSP
-      {"milmb", &hybrid_andes_csr::milmb},          // F5
+      {"mecc_code", &hybrid_andes_csr::mecc_code},  // F5 memory system
       {"mpft_ctl", &hybrid_andes_csr::mpft_ctl},    // F6
       {"mhsp_ctl", &hybrid_andes_csr::mhsp_ctl},    // F7
       {"mcountermask_m", &hybrid_andes_csr::mcountermask_m},  // F8
@@ -341,6 +342,18 @@ int main() {
     CHECK(diff_states(ref, got).ok());
   }
 
+  {  // milmb/mdlmb are the ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs. The base address matches
+     // across engines, but the enable bit (bit 0) is HW-presence state: the vsim
+     // RTL has the local memories and drains EN=1, while QEMU models none and
+     // drains EN=0. Same engine-reset-divergent class as msp_bound/msp_base, so
+     // verify EXCLUDES them -- still transported, just not strict-compared.
+    const hybrid_state_v1 ref = andes_state();
+    hybrid_state_v1 got = ref;
+    got.andes.milmb ^= 0x1;  // flip the enable bit only (base unchanged)
+    got.andes.mdlmb ^= 0x1;
+    CHECK(diff_states(ref, got).ok());
+  }
+
   {  // S4 Andes caps: a CSR the engine does NOT implement is verify-excluded.
      // vsim never restored/re-read it (the resume/drain gate), so comparing it
      // against the QEMU oracle would false-diff. The supported list comes from
diff --git a/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh b/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh
index 21f5a0e..f80ea47 100755
--- a/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh
+++ b/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh
@@ -25,7 +25,9 @@ printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
   || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
 ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"
 
-# --- B. cycle: rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run -------
+# --- B. rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run --------------
+#   cycle uses the shared ELF/engine arch check; hybrid rejects it even earlier
+#   (its QEMU fast leg is rv64-only). Both exit 2 with a clear error, no run.
 if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
   out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
         --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
@@ -33,8 +35,15 @@ if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
   printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
     || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
   ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
+
+  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
+        --trigger marker --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "the hybrid fast leg (QEMU) is rv64-only" \
+    || fail "hybrid rv64-on-rv32 missing the clear error: $out"
+  ok "hybrid: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> rv64-only fast-leg error, no run"
 else
-  ok "SKIP cycle rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
+  ok "SKIP rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
 fi
 
 # --- C. rv32 directions: need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 to build an rv32 fixture -----
@@ -66,7 +75,9 @@ else
   ok "SKIP rv32 run: no qemu-system-riscv32 under $QD"
 fi
 
-# cycle: the rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error.
+# rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error. The rv64 engine
+# clears hybrid's rv64-only fast-leg guard, so the rv32 ELF reaches the same
+# shared elf_engine_arch_error in BOTH cycle and hybrid.
 rv64eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim" && $4=="64"{print $1; exit}')
 if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
   out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
@@ -75,6 +86,13 @@ if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
   printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
     || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
   ok "cycle: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
+
+  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
+        --trigger marker --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
+  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
+    || fail "hybrid rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
+  ok "hybrid: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
 else
-  ok "SKIP cycle rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
+  ok "SKIP rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
 fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1+F3 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the driver respects the ELF's class (rv32/rv64).
#   - fast  auto-picks qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (and runs it).
#   - cycle/hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen, both ways,
#     with one shared clear error and WITHOUT launching the engine.
# Independent, gated sections: rv64 always; the rv32 directions need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (build the rv32 fixture) and skip cleanly without it.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF"

BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)

# --- A. fast: an rv64 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv64 (no --engine) ------
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"

# --- B. rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run --------------
#   cycle uses the shared ELF/engine arch check; hybrid rejects it even earlier
#   (its QEMU fast leg is rv64-only). Both exit 2 with a clear error, no run.
if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
    || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"

  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
        --trigger marker --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "the hybrid fast leg (QEMU) is rv64-only" \
    || fail "hybrid rv64-on-rv32 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "hybrid: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> rv64-only fast-leg error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
fi

# --- C. rv32 directions: need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 to build an rv32 fixture -----
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 directions: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
# Only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 -- the rv32 fixture build must not need the rv64 one.
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
rv32elf="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rv32_c_hello.elf"
[ -f "$rv32elf" ] || fail "rv32 fixture missing after build: $rv32elf"

# fast: the rv32 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv32.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv32' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv32 for an rv32 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv32 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv32"

# fast: and it actually runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime end to end).
QD=$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)
if [ -x "$QD/qemu-system-riscv32" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hello from QEMU1' \
    || fail "rv32 fixture did not run/print on qemu-system-riscv32: $out"
  ok "fast: rv32 fixture runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime works)"
else
  ok "SKIP rv32 run: no qemu-system-riscv32 under $QD"
fi

# rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error. The rv64 engine
# clears hybrid's rv64-only fast-leg guard, so the rv32 ELF reaches the same
# shared elf_engine_arch_error in BOTH cycle and hybrid.
rv64eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim" && $4=="64"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
    || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"

  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
        --trigger marker --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
    || fail "hybrid rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "hybrid: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
fi

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

Clean analysis done. One concrete reuse finding, plus one minor note.

## Findings

**1. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` lines 39-44 and 90-95 — new hybrid blocks re-implement the `expect` helper**

Both new hybrid blocks hand-roll the exact "run a command, assert exit code, assert output matches" sequence that `tests/lib/log.sh` already provides as `expect <rc> <re> CMD..` (defined at log.sh:14, already sourced here at line 12, already used by sibling `test_andes_sim_f9.sh:42-49`).

Each new block duplicates: `out=$(... 2>&1); rc=$?` + `[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail ...` + `printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q ... || fail ...`. That is precisely `expect`'s body.

Call instead, e.g. for lines 39-44:
```sh
expect 2 "the hybrid fast leg \(QEMU\) is rv64-only" \
  timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
  --trigger marker --engine vsim:d23 "$elf"
ok "hybrid: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> rv64-only fast-leg error, no run"
```
And lines 90-95 map cleanly with no escaping (the `ELF is rv32 but engine '...' is rv64` string has no ERE metacharacters):
```sh
expect 2 "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
  timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
  --trigger marker --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf"
```
Caveat: `expect` uses `grep -Eq`, so the `(QEMU)` literal must be escaped to `\(QEMU\)`. Note the pre-existing cycle blocks (lines 32-37, 83-88) carry the same smell, but those predate this diff.

**2. (Minor/optional) `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` lines 345-355 — new milmb/mdlmb block duplicates the msp_bound/msp_base block above it**

The new exclusion test is structurally identical to the immediately preceding block (lines 335-343): `ref = andes_state()`, mutate the excluded fields, `CHECK(diff_states(ref, got).ok())`. Both assert the same property (excluded CSR -> still ok). Could be folded into the one block. No reusable helper exists for this though, and the separation reads as deliberate per-CSR-class documentation, so this is weak — flag only if you want fewer near-identical blocks.

## Clean (checked, not issues)
- `state_diff.cpp` `andes_verify_excluded`: adding `milmb`/`mdlmb` to the `name == ...` chain is the established mechanism here; no helper is being re-implemented.
- `kAndesCompared = (13 - 4) + ...`: the `13` literal is pre-existing hardcoding (diff only bumps `2`->`4`). There is no Andes-list count macro to reuse (only `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM` exists for the M-ext list), so nothing new is duplicated.
